```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6
)
library(SpaceMosaic)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(spatialdataR)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
```

# Overview

The workflow is:

1. define the response-cell subset and design variable(s) ($X$);
2. encode the cellular microenvironment ($Z$);
3. identify and quality-control spatially contiguous patches;
4. estimate within-patch expression associations;
5. borrow information among patches with similar contexts ($W$); and
6. interpret recurrent or context-specific effects in space.

This vignette repeats the analysis of the `SpatialExperiment` case study, but
on a `SpatialData` object. A `SpatialData` object keeps the cell geometries
and the expression data in separate elements:

- shapes: cell geometries (here, one point per cell) in
  `shapes(sd)[[shape]]`, from which spatial coordinates are taken;
- tables: a `SingleCellExperiment` in `tables(sd)[[table]]` that annotates a
  shapes element and holds
  - expression: assay **genes x cells**;
  - $X$: column or columns in colData **cells x predictors**;
  - $Z$: an embedding stored in reducedDims **cells x neighborhood features**;
- $W$: patch-level attributes derived from $Z$ by `patchMetaAnalysis.sd()`
  (**patches x patch features**), returned alongside the meta-analysis results
  rather than stored back on `sd`.

The `.sd`-suffixed functions used below (`embedCellNeighborhoods.sd()`,
`getPatches.sd()`, `patchDE.sd()`, `patchMetaAnalysis.sd()`,
`moranTest.sd()`) are `SpatialData` wrappers: they read $X$, $Z$, expression,
and patch assignments from the table selected with the `table` argument, and
spatial coordinates from the shapes element that table annotates.
`embedCellNeighborhoods.sd()` and `getPatches.sd()` attach their results back
onto `sd` and return it; `getPatches.sd()` also stores the patch polygons as a
new shapes element. `patchDE.sd()` returns its differential-expression results
alongside `sd` (whose table also gains a `"residuals"` assay when
`return_residuals = TRUE`); and `patchMetaAnalysis.sd()` returns the
meta-analysis results (`meta` and `W`, plus `subgroups_summary` when
requested) without `sd`.

# Data and analysis question

Single-cell spatial transcriptomics (6k-plex CosMx SMI) dataset of human
basal-cell carcinoma from https://zenodo.org/records/14330691 was preprocessed
before the analysis. The original Seurat object was converted to a
`SpatialExperiment` object, and data was filtered for Patient A and FOVs 39 to
41. This consists of a nodular-ulcerated BCC sample.

`spe_to_spatialdata()` converts it to a `SpatialData` object: the spatial
coordinates become the points of the shapes element `shape1`, and everything
else (assays, colData, reducedDims) becomes the table `table` annotating it.

```{r load-data}
spe <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cosmx_carcinoma.rds", package = "SpaceMosaic"))
sd <- spe_to_spatialdata(spe)
sd
```

The shapes are stored in a DuckDB table whose row order is not guaranteed, so
cells are always matched to their geometries by identifier. The helper below
returns the coordinates of the cells of a table, in the order of its columns,
using the `cell_id` column that `spe_to_spatialdata()` stores in the shapes.

```{r cell-coords}
cellCoords <- function(sd, shape, sce) {
  cells <- st_as_sf(data(shapes(sd)[[shape]]))
  xy <- st_coordinates(cells)[match(colnames(sce), cells$cell_id), ]
  rownames(xy) <- colnames(sce)
  xy
}
```

We study the exposure of Cancer Cells near Fibroblasts.

```{r define-x}
# Example: distance to the nearest cell of a selected explanatory population.
sce <- table(sd)
xy <- cellCoords(sd, "shape1", sce)

distance_to_explanatory <- FNN::get.knnx(
  data = xy[sce$celltype == "Fibroblast", ],
  query = xy,
  k = 1
)$nn.dist[, 1]

sce$distance <- log1p(distance_to_explanatory)
table(sd) <- sce
```

# Cellular-neighborhood embedding ($Z$)

`embedCellNeighborhoods()` averages a cell-level embedding over spatial
neighbor networks at multiple scales. Compute $Z$ on all cells before taking
the response-cell subset, so the representation retains the surrounding
tissue context. Supply `tissue` when the object contains multiple samples,
slides, or fields of view; this prevents neighborhoods from crossing tissue
boundaries.

```{r cellular-neighborhoods}
sd <- embedCellNeighborhoods.sd(
  sd = sd,
  embedding = 'PCA',
  ks = c(5, 50),
  tissue = 'sample_id'
)

head(reducedDim(table(sd), "Z")[, 1:5], 3)
```

# Response-cell subset

Patches are built on the response cells only. Replacing `table` with a subset
of its cells would make `spatialdataR` drop the geometries of the remaining
cells from `shape1`, so we instead add the cancer cells as a separate
shapes/table pair, `cancer_shape` and `cancer_cells`, carrying over $X$ and
$Z$ computed above. We convert them to a new `SpatialData` object and merge it
into `sd` with `combine()` from `spatialdataR`. The shapes element and the
table must have different names.

```{r define-subset}
sce <- table(sd)
use <- sce$celltype == "Cancer.cells"

spe_use <- spe[, use]
spe_use$distance <- sce$distance[use]
reducedDim(spe_use, "Z") <- reducedDim(sce, "Z")[use, ]

sd_use <- spe_to_spatialdata(
  spe_use,
  shape_name = "cancer_shape",
  table_name = "cancer_cells"
)
sd <- combine(sd, sd_use)
sd
```

From here on, every wrapper is called with `table = "cancer_cells"`.

# Patch identification and quality control

`getPatches()` favors spatially compact, contiguous regions that retain
within-patch variation in $X$ while remaining coherent in $Z$.

```{r identify-patches}
set.seed(123)

X = 'distance'
sd <- getPatches.sd(
  sd,
  X = X,
  Z = 'Z',
  npatches = 100,       # CHANGE for tissue area and response-cell abundance
  alpha = 0.5,          # weight of the Z-coherence penalty
  beta = 1,   # weight of within-patch X diversity
  hunger_weight = 0.5, # balances patch size and X variation
  max_elongation = 4,
  mahal_radius = 3,
  n_candidates = 20,
  n_iters = 5,
  log_iters = TRUE,
  table = "cancer_cells"
)

sce_use <- table(sd, "cancer_cells")

plotPatchIterations(
  xy = cellCoords(sd, "cancer_shape", sce_use),
  result = metadata(sce_use)$SpaceMosaic$patch_iterations,
  iters = 1:5,
  ask = FALSE
)
```


Patch diagnostics stored in the metadata of the table report assignment
coverage and summarize patch size, within-patch variation in `X`, spatial
connectivity, and final membership stability. These are general checks; RNA
content, distance to an explanatory population, tissue region, and sample
identity can reveal additional experiment-specific failure modes.

```{r patch-diagnostics}

patch_diagnostics <- metadata(sce_use)$SpaceMosaic$patch_diagnostics

# CHANGE to the X column that should be inspected when X is multivariable.
x_sd_column <- if (length(X) == 1L) "x_sd" else paste0("x_sd_", X[1])
patch_diagnostics$selected_x_sd <- patch_diagnostics[[x_sd_column]]
patch_diagnostics$connectivity <- factor(
  ifelse(
    patch_diagnostics$strict_component_fraction == 1,
    "Connected",
    "Fragmented"
  ),
  levels = c("Connected", "Fragmented")
)

# CHANGE after inspecting the diagnostic distributions and predictor scale.
min_cells <- 30
min_x_sd <- 0.1
min_stability <- 0.9

ggplot(patch_diagnostics, aes(n_cells, selected_x_sd)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = membership_stability, shape = connectivity), size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min_cells, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = min_x_sd, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey70") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Connected = 21, Fragmented = 24)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Core patch diagnostics",
    x = "Cells per patch",
    y = "Within-patch standard deviation of X",
    fill = "Membership stability",
    shape = "Connectivity"
  )

keep <- with(
  patch_diagnostics,
  patch[
    n_cells >= min_cells &
      is.finite(selected_x_sd) & selected_x_sd >= min_x_sd &
      !is.na(membership_stability) &
      membership_stability >= min_stability &
      strict_component_fraction == 1
  ]
)

sce_use$patch[!sce_use$patch %in% keep] <- NA
table(sd, "cancer_cells") <- sce_use
```

The plot combines patch size, predictor variation, final stability, and
connectivity; crosses mark fragmentation at `strict_k`. Replace the
example thresholds after inspecting the dataset and the scale of `X`, then set
cells in excluded patches to `NA` in the table as shown above.

`getPatches.sd()` stored one polygon per patch, annotated with the patch
diagnostics, in the shapes element `patch_polys`. It still holds every patch;
the excluded ones are dropped after converting it to an `sf` object.

```{r patch-polys}
polys <- st_as_sf(data(shapes(sd)$patch_polys))
polys <- polys[polys$patch %in% keep, ]
head(polys)
```

Overlay the retained patch boundaries on the per-cell map of $X$ to check
visually that patches trace coherent regions of the exposure variable rather
than cutting across it.

```{r patch-map}
sce <- table(sd)
cells <- st_as_sf(data(shapes(sd)$shape1))
cells$distance_use <- ifelse(
  sce$celltype == "Cancer.cells",
  sce$distance,
  NA
)[match(cells$cell_id, colnames(sce))]

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = cells, aes(color = distance_use), size = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = polys, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distance to nearest Fibroblast",
    x = "x",
    y = "y",
    color = "log1p(distance)"
  )
```

# Within-patch differential expression

`patchDE.sd()` wraps `patchDE()` for a `SpatialData` object: it takes the
assay named by `assay` (genes x cells) from the selected table, transposes it
internally, builds the predictor data frame from `predictor_cols` in its
colData, and reads patch assignments from its `patch_column`; cells with a
missing patch assignment are dropped automatically.

For raw counts, `pearson = TRUE` computes Pearson residuals separately within
each patch and requires `tot` to name a colData column holding per-cell total
counts. Alternatively, transform or normalize expression before calling
`patchDE.sd()` and include relevant technical covariates in `predictor_cols`.

```{r patch-de}
de_result <- patchDE.sd(
  sd = sd,
  predictor_cols = 'distance',
  method = "limma",
  pearson = FALSE,
  tot = 'total',
  return_residuals = TRUE,
  table = "cancer_cells"
)
```

# Borrowing information across patches ($W$)

`patchMetaAnalysis.sd()` derives patch-level attributes ($W$) by averaging
the embedding named by `embedding_name` (default `"Z"`, taken from the
reducedDims of the table) within each patch, then borrows information across
patches with similar $W$ by running `patchMetaAnalysis()` on the per-patch
fits produced by `patchDE.sd()`. It uses the same table as `patchDE.sd()`
unless `table` is given. Set `summarize_subgroups = TRUE` to also summarize
effects within subgroups of patches, optionally annotated with
`cellmeta_cols` taken from the colData of the table.

```{r patch-meta}
meta_result <- patchMetaAnalysis.sd(
  patchDE_result = de_result,
  summarize_subgroups = TRUE,
  cellmeta_cols = c("celltype", "distance")
)
```



# Result summaries and spatial validation

Rank genes using a criterion chosen in advance. The example below uses the
fraction of patches with an absolute posterior Z-score above 2. Effect sizes,
posterior p-values, subgroup membership, and biological relevance should also
be considered; very small p-values alone are not sufficient.

```{r result-summary}
z_score <- meta_result$meta$distance$ests/ meta_result$meta$distance$ses

gene_summary <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(z_score),
  recurrent = rowMeans(abs(z_score) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
  positive = rowMeans(z_score > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
  negative = rowMeans(z_score < -2, na.rm = TRUE)
)
gene_summary <- gene_summary[
  order(gene_summary$recurrent, decreasing = TRUE),
]
top_genes <- head(gene_summary$gene, 50)

heatmap(
  z_score[top_genes, , drop = FALSE],
  scale = "none"
)
```


`return_residuals = TRUE` stored the within-patch residuals as a
`"residuals"` assay of the `cancer_cells` table of `de_result$sd`, which
`moranTest.sd()` reads directly. To test only the top genes, replace that
table by its subset of rows; cells, and therefore the shapes it annotates, are
left untouched.

```{r moran}
sd_moran <- de_result$sd
table(sd_moran, "cancer_cells") <- table(sd_moran, "cancer_cells")[top_genes, ]

moran_test <- moranTest.sd(
  sd_moran,
  k = 20,
  n_permutations = 20,
  table = "cancer_cells"
)

head(moran_test[order(moran_test$observed, decreasing = TRUE),])
```

Finally, project representative effects back onto the tissue. Confirm that
their direction agrees with the predictor and is not driven by an unmodeled
sample, anatomical compartment, low-quality region, or segmentation artifact.

```{r spatial-validation}
gene <- top_genes[1]
poly_gene <- polys
poly_gene$z_score <- z_score[gene, ][as.character(poly_gene$patch)]

ggplot(poly_gene) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = z_score), color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = gene, fill = "Posterior Z")

```
